method: Facts gathered through web search (search results only; pages could not be opened) on Nov. 27, 2026. Ratings are the latest Cook Political Report rating found; Cook's closing table was paywalled, so seven Toss-ups are inferred from its closing analysis (seven Toss-ups, six held by Republicans) and its Aug. 20, Oct. 6 and Oct. 20 changes.
gaps: Cook final ratings: the closing-analysis table was not retrievable (paywalled; fetching blocked). Toss-ups (AK, IA, KS, ME, MI, OH, TX) are inferred from the closing analysis's count ('seven races in Toss Up, six held by Republicans') plus the Aug 20 ratings page and the Oct 6 and Oct 20 changes. Solid ratings come from Cook's Aug 20, 2026 page and were not individually re-confirmed at close.
FL: final Cook rating not confirmed (Solid R on race page last updated Feb 2025; a later shift toward the challenger was reported but its category was not shown). rating.rating is null.
NE: the Lean R move date is unknown; the source is secondary (cryptobriefing), corroborated by Sabato/Inside Lean R as of Oct 27 (Ballotpedia).
GA Likely D (Sept 23) and MN Lean D (Oct 20) rest on secondary reporting; MN sequence reported inconsistently.
ID: Democratic nominee (if any) not identified; independent Todd Achilles was the main challenger.
SD: Democratic candidate's withdrawal not verified; independent Brian Bengs was the challenger.

OK: Mullin's resignation (Mar 24, 2026) and the Alan Armstrong appointment come from a single source. Not checked whether a separate special election for the remainder of the term was also held. Hern's 57.2% is from an aggregator.
SC: not checked whether a separate special election for the remainder of Graham's term also took place. The date of Santee Cooper's data center rate action is unconfirmed.
ME: whether Gov. Mills signed LD 307 (data center moratorium) not confirmed.
DE: the report that the Project Washington developer dropped its appeal (Aug 2026) comes from a search summary; WHYY source covers the DNREC setback.

Signals not searched (budget): aiSignal and stateSignal for ID, MA, RI, SD, OK; aiSignal for FL. aiSignal null for AL, AR, CO, DE, IL, KY, LA, MN, NJ, NM, OR, TN, WV, WY means none found in limited searches (often not specifically searched), not proof of absence.
AK and IA aiSignals are weak (news framing, not direct candidate statements). MI's strongest evidence is from the primary; for the general, NPR cites El-Sayed's 'terms of engagement' stance.
Most vote shares are unofficial/early counts; certification status not checked. WV result relies on Legis1 citing AP.
Overall: Democrats flipped 9 R-held seats (AK, IA, KS, ME, MS, NC, OH, SC, TX) with no D losses, which matches Wikipedia's 56-seat Democratic caucus; not cross-checked against an official tally.
All facts come from search-result summaries (page fetching blocked). Several rest on a single secondary source and should be spot-checked before publication.
